answers.core:
It needs to touch `Node3D`'s transform directly and integrate with the
existing group system already in `SceneTree` — there's no extension point
an addon could hook to intercept "just shifted the whole world" in a way
every downstream system (physics, particles, custom renderers) could
consistently rely on. An addon can (and today, does) reimplement the
node-shifting loop itself, but it can't give other addons/games a single
shared signal to converge on, which is the actual value: right now every
project's floating-origin implementation is a bespoke, incompatible
one-off.
answers.workaround:
It *is* currently worked around this way in every project that needs it —
that's the problem. I've independently built this exact pattern twice: once
as `Terrain3D::rebase()` (github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D PR #1019,
region-coordinate-based, since merged/positively reviewed — deferred to
Terrain3D 1.2 pending their own region-streaming work, not rejected on
design) for a GDExtension module, and once as a plain GDScript
`world_origin.gd` singleton in my own project (signal-based, no grid
alignment needed since content there regenerates from true position rather
than being stored at an address). Both hand-rolled implementations converge
on the same shape: an offset, a rebase entry point, and a signal for
non-tree-derived systems to react to. That convergence, independently
arrived at twice, is what suggests this belongs at the engine level rather
than being reinvented per-project.
